National Resistance Army.question: The _____ was Military wing of the National Resistance Movement (NRM) of Uganda (1981–1995).
National Resistance Army.fact: The National Resistance Army (NRA) was a guerilla army and the military wing of the National Resistance Movement (NRM) that fought in the Ugandan Bush War against the government of Milton Obote, and later the government of Tito Okello.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: NRA was supported by _____
National Resistance Army.fact: NRA was supported by Muammar Gaddafi.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: NRA was formed in _____ when Yoweri Museveni's Popular Resistance Army (PRA) merged with ex-president Yusuf Lule's group, the Uganda Freedom Fighters (UFF)
National Resistance Army.fact: NRA was formed in 1981 when Yoweri Museveni's Popular Resistance Army (PRA) merged with ex-president Yusuf Lule's group, the Uganda Freedom Fighters (UFF).

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: Museveni, then leader of the Uganda Patriotic Movement party, alleged electoral fraud and declared an armed rebellion, following the victory of Uganda Peoples Congress in the bitterly disputed _____ g
National Resistance Army.fact: Museveni, then leader of the Uganda Patriotic Movement party, alleged electoral fraud and declared an armed rebellion, following the victory of Uganda Peoples Congress in the bitterly disputed 1980 general election.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: By the time the victorious NRA entered Kampala in _____, about a quarter of its 16,000 combatants were Banyarwanda, while Fred Rwigema was its deputy commander
National Resistance Army.fact: Museveni, who had guerrilla war experience with the Mozambican Liberation Front (FRELIMO) in Mozambique, and his own Front for National Salvation (FRONASA) formed in Tanzania to fight Idi Amin, led the NRA to victory against Ugandan government troops (UNLA) in 1986. By the time the victorious NRA entered Kampala in 1986, about a quarter of its 16,000 combatants were Banyarwanda, while Fred Rwigema was its deputy commander.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: Shortly afterwards, the UNLA carried out a number of attacks against civilians in the north of _____
National Resistance Army.fact: Museveni, who had guerrilla war experience with the Mozambican Liberation Front (FRELIMO) in Mozambique, and his own Front for National Salvation (FRONASA) formed in Tanzania to fight Idi Amin, led the NRA to victory against Ugandan government troops (UNLA) in 1986. Shortly afterwards, the UNLA carried out a number of attacks against civilians in the north of Uganda.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: The attacks largely targeted the Acholi people and were in part seen as a form of revenge for _____, the scorched-earth operation there that had been ordered by Milton Obote during his presidency
National Resistance Army.fact: The attacks largely targeted the Acholi people and were in part seen as a form of revenge for Operation Bonanza, the scorched-earth operation there that had been ordered by Milton Obote during his presidency.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: From _____ to 1990, the Museveni regime tried to end various insurgencies and establish control over the army
National Resistance Army.fact: From 1986 to 1990, the Museveni regime tried to end various insurgencies and establish control over the army.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: Despite repeated government claims that the NRA had defeated the _____ and other rebel groups, insurgent activity continued, especially in the northern, eastern, and western regions
National Resistance Army.fact: Shortly afterwards, the UNLA carried out a number of attacks against civilians in the north of Uganda. Despite repeated government claims that the NRA had defeated the UNLA and other rebel groups, insurgent activity continued, especially in the northern, eastern, and western regions.

National Resistance Army.subject: Environment & Ecology
National Resistance Army.question: In April _____, 3,000 former Uganda People's Army (UPA) fighters and members of several other small rebel groups accepted a government amnesty by surrendering and declaring their support for Museveni'
National Resistance Army.fact: In April 1988, 3,000 former Uganda People's Army (UPA) fighters and members of several other small rebel groups accepted a government amnesty by surrendering and declaring their support for Museveni's regime. In June 1988, the president concluded a peace agreement with Uganda People's Democratic Army (UPDA) commander Lieutenant Colonel John Angelo Okello.
